en: The Apadāna of the Elder Saḷalapupphiya Mandāravapupphiya Chapter 10 I offered a saḷala flower to the Buddha, the Great Sage, the Teacher of the World, who was endowed with the ten powers. Because of that deed, I have attained the fruit of Arhatship; I am now free from all defilements and have reached the final state. I have lived the holy life and accomplished my task; there is no further existence for me. This is my last birth. I shall not undergo further rebirth. “On the bank of the Candabhāgā River,
I was then a kinnara;
there I saw the God of Gods.”
To the Bull among Men as he was walking to and fro,
I plucked a *saḷala* flower and gave it to the Buddha.
The Great Hero inhaled the *saḷala* flower, fragrant as the gods;
having accepted it, the Fully Awakened One—
Vipassī, the leader of the world,
the Great Hero, sniffed [the air] while I was looking on.
With a clear mind and joyful heart,
having paid homage to the Supreme among Bipeds and raising his hands in reverential salutation, he spoke.
Again I ascended the mountain;
in the ninety-first aeon,
I offered this flower in worship.
I do not know a state of woe;
this is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha.
The four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā) [are mine].
the Buddha’s teaching has been fulfilled.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Saḷalapupphiya speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Saḷalapupphiya is the tenth.
The Mandāravapupphiya Chapter is the thirty-seventh. Its summary (uddāna) is as follows:
Mandārava and kakkāru,
bhisaka and kesara-pupphiya;
aṅkolaka and kadambī.
Uddālī and Ekacampaka;
Timira and Saḷala,
and likewise the Gāthā and Tālīsaka.
